executiveSummary: Borger-Odoorn's official 2025 administrative, demographic and regional inputs reconcile, and the mandatory deterministic contract passes all ten presets, six checkpoints and eight essential services. The result is not yet safe as a locally realistic first-72-hour decision layer. The coastal preset shows zero direct inundation, zero headline and peak severity, and an explanation that no event forcing is active, while its 19.37 m/s wind still creates 1,137 affected people-equivalent and 25,558 event-attributable service person-hours at T+24; this directly conflicts with the displayed causal account and obscures VRD's distinction between no direct Drenthe sea-flood consequence and an evacuation/reception role. Six unrelated hazards also produce the same exact 58-neighbourhood order, and an explicit fire source in Exloo Buitengebied ranks only eleventh behind locations 5–12 km away. Public water, provider, antenna, transport, education and acute-care data can improve context immediately, but they do not expose the sensitive topology, operational state, capacity, backup or restoration needed to calibrate utility behavior. Those gaps remain Unknown, not zero, and all exact impact/recovery values remain deterministic exercise outputs.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK
evidenceSources.title: E01 — Official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood and demographic inputs
supports: GM1681 identity, generalized boundary and centre containment
Companion CBS OData 86165NED statistics: population 26,049, density 95, 26.8 percent aged 65 or older and 3,493 one-person households
Fifty-eight neighbourhoods and explicit missing-value semantics
CBS inputs are CC BY 4.0; the generated BAG place layer is Public Domain Mark 1.0 and BRT TOP10NL is CC BY 4.0

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Omgevingsvisie BuitenGewoon: Duurzaam in alles
supports: Extreme rain and flooding alternate with heat and drought
The rural water system must discharge, retain and store water, with groundwater levels and peat-area dust storms material
Hunze en Aa's, Vechtstromen and WMD are named partners
Electricity grid capacity is an important local constraint, but not an outage-probability observation

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025
supports: Drenthe risk context for extreme rain, storm, heat, drought, nature fire, vital-service disruption, cyber and induced earthquakes
A 70 mm/hour cloudburst can inundate streets, cellars, houses and low roads
Drenthe has no primary sea- or major-river defences; direct sea-flood consequences do not apply and the region instead prepares to receive evacuees, people and animals
Limited large-water risk is associated with the Meppel area and may indirectly disrupt vital functions and road or rail
Heat increases peak drinking-water demand and mortality particularly among older residents; drought affects sand, peat, infrastructure and firefighting water

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Crisisplan Veiligheidsregio Drenthe 2026–2029
supports: CoPI starts its tasks within 30 minutes after alarming and focuses on the incident and operational effects
ROT supports continuity, medium-to-long-term scenarios and allocation of scarce operational resources
Information management, operational leadership, mayoral authority and water-board or other partner participation are role-specific
The plan defines a flexible crisis organisation, not a guaranteed 72-hour intervention script or restoration service level

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Hunze en Aa's / Het Waterschapshuis
evidenceSources.title: E05 — Waterbeheerprogramma 2022–2027 and public IMWA/DAMO registers
supports: Hunze and Veenkoloniën are distinct water systems with different discharge, retention, storage and freshwater mechanisms
The generated HWH/PDOK point-in-polygon context finds 270 registered assets in GM1681: 247 weirs, 13 sewer pumps, eight surface-water pumps, one sluice and one wastewater-treatment plant
IMWA Kunstwerken and DAMO Waterketen OGC APIs are CC BY-SA 4.0, provider-supplied and incomplete by contributor; object dates vary
Public point capacity fields in this snapshot do not carry a unit and cannot be used as causal throughput

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Risico Index Natuurbranden
supports: RIN combines seventeen parameters into risk per square kilometre for preparation and mitigation
RIN is the preferred authoritative nature-fire context, but no public bulk API, redistribution licence or fixed update cadence was found
Staatsbosbeheer separately identifies the 1,850 hectare Exloo-Odoorn and 2,900 hectare Gieten-Borger forest areas within the Hondsrug context

evidenceSources.title: E07 — KNMI earthquake catalogue
supports: Machine-readable induced and tectonic event records are available as JSON, CSV and KML and update automatically when KNMI publishes an event
A selected observed event is context, not a probability or a calibrated municipality damage scenario
KNMI five-minute radar composites under CC BY 4.0 are an integration-ready observed-rainfall source, but must be time-aligned to an event before affecting the simulation

evidenceSources.title: E08 — Vragenlijst aanbod SEH's en Acute Verloskunde 2026
supports: No acute hospital is inside GM1681 in the current CC0 questionnaire-derived layer

Treant Scheper Emmen is the nearest listed site by 13.38 km straight-line reference-point distance and reports a 24/7 emergency department, acute obstetrics, sixteen treatment rooms and 22,589 visits in 2025
The survey is dated facility-role context, not live occupancy, staffing, diversion, generator endurance or incident capacity

identity.summary: The generated identifier, name, province and safety-region assignment match the official 2025 inputs.
notes: Feature id, regional bundle code and bundle name all equal GM1681 / Borger-Odoorn.
The CBS safety-region layer assigns GM1681 uniquely to Drenthe.

geography.summary: The application consumes the official 2025 generalized boundary and its municipality centre is inside it.
notes: Administrative containment does not validate terrain, catchments, fire fuels, utility service areas or hazard footprints.

demography.summary: Municipality and neighbourhood 2025 population values reconcile within CBS five-person rounding.
notes: Official municipality population is 26,049; 58 published neighbourhood values sum to 26,040, a difference of nine people (-0.035 percent).
Density is 95, the age-65-plus share is 26.8 percent, one-person households are 3,493, neighbourhood households sum to 11,620 and rounded age-65-plus counts sum to 6,980.
These aggregate values describe population context and never identify individual vulnerability or preparedness.

regionalDetail.summary: All 58 official neighbourhood rows and 36 supported fields load, but incomplete fields remain null and the spatial statistics are not hazard surfaces.
notes: Core population, household and age fields have 58/58 coverage; doctor and supermarket distance have 56/58, cars per household 43/58 and several housing/benefit fields 53/58.
District-heating percentage and public-charging-point fields have 0/58 usable values. They remain missing, not zero.
The official zero-population neighbourhood 1e Exloërmond Buitengebied remains exactly zero in all local allocations.

settlements.summary: Twenty-five BAG places and 31 BRT TOP10NL settlements resolve without place-centre leakage from the generalized boundary.
notes: The BRT set contains fifteen woonkernen, thirteen buurtschappen, two deelkernen and one gehucht; its source date is 2025-07-01 and geometry is unsimplified.
Settlement source population metadata is descriptive and is not required to sum to the CBS municipality total.

transport.summary: Official road, rail and transit context is inspectable, but the eight-link graph is a logical proxy with no live capacity or closure state.
notes: Eight NWB links connect four neighbours through N34, N366, N374, N379 and N857; all are labeled regional with the same synthetic nominal capacity 150.
No ProRail station lies inside the boundary; 139 GTFS stop areas include P+R Borger, but static stops and schedules are not vehicles, passenger capacity, accessibility or live operation.
The deployment-time NDW snapshot contained no qualifying point records inside GM1681. No record is Unknown operational state, not evidence that every road is open.

emergencyContext.summary: The correct VRD roles and 72-hour planning horizon are documented, but actual local decisions, resources, facilities and continuity status are not modeled.
notes: VRD distinguishes incident command, medium/long-term continuity and scarcity coordination, mayoral authority, water-board participation and information management.
No acute hospital is inside GM1681; route-aware access to Emmen is therefore material, but the model contains no ambulance dispatch, acceptance or diversion state.
Eighteen DUO education locations and five government/service registry points are public context, not verified shelters, command posts, support points or live capacity.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical scenarios execute, but the coastal preset's zero-severity causal account contradicts its event-attributable service impacts.
notes: The required matrix ran severe storm, pluvial flood, river flood, coastal flood, heatwave, winter storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.
Maximum current severity at those checkpoints is storm 0.7750, pluvial 0.3296, river 0, coastal 0, heat 0.5157, winter 0.5997, cyber 0.4948, earthquake 0.2226, wildfire 0.1343 and compound 0.9119.

At coastal T+24 direct water, headline severity and peak severity are zero, yet wind is 19.37 m/s, pressure 0.1710, affected population 1,137 and cumulative event-attributable service burden 25,558.43 person-hours.

At compound T+24 pressure is 0.5613 with 15,464 affected and 248,542.59 person-hours; at T+72 inundation stress is 0.5194, pressure 0.6489, affected 18,678 and cumulative burden 1,028,983.74. These are scenario estimates, not observations or forecasts.

numericalInvariants.summary: The focused gate passes boundedness, exact-zero, deterministic, causal, population and service reconciliation contracts.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM1681 pnpm audit:model passed both tests before artifact creation across 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services.
Every intensity-zero preset has exactly zero current severity, peak severity, affected population and event-attributable person-hours at every checkpoint.
All local maps allocate exactly 26,049 people, retain the official zero population, and reconcile service demand/delivery within 2.85e-14.
Switching among all service/map layers leaves the local hazard field exactly invariant; cumulative person-hours are monotonic and route flows remain within logical capacity.

spatialPlausibility.summary: One shared neighbourhood seed ignores hazard mechanisms, and an explicit local fire source does not control the fire ranking.
notes: At T+24 severe storm, pluvial flood, heatwave, winter storm, cyberattack and wildfire have the identical exact order of all 58 neighbourhoods, starting Borger Buitengebied, 2e Valthermond, Oud Borger, Borger-Centrum and Drouwenermond Buitengebied.
The ranking samples no AHN height/depression, catchment, paving/shade, peat, forest/fuel, wind direction, road exposure, provider asset or cyber target.

In a focused synthetic T+24 fire with source [6.843571882747512, 52.88604611537499] at Exloo Buitengebied's official centre, municipality severity is 0.6026, direct fire 0.5868, smoke 0.6002 and drought 0.6966.

Source neighbourhood Exloo Buitengebied ranks 11/58 at 0.6791. Borger Buitengebied 6.639 km away ranks first at 0.7105; the remaining top four are 5.146–11.864 km away. This is a synthetic reproduction, not an observed incident.
Canonical wildfire uses an epicentre 111.247 km from the municipality centre, gives zero direct flame and 0.2533 smoke at T+24; that scoped output cannot be read as absence of a local fire.

serviceDependencies.summary: All eight balances and dependency stages are inspectable, but none is calibrated to GM1681's actual operators, water controls, telecom, roads or care system.
notes: Live public-domain territory lookup at the municipality reference point returns Enexis electricity/gas, WMD drinking water and Ziggo fixed media; drainage returns no polygon, which remains Unknown rather than no responsible authority.

The public app context has 270 HWH water assets and 86 RDI antenna sites representing 171 antennas, but these are non-causal points and do not establish connectivity, capacity units, state, coverage, backhaul, power backup or restoration.

All eight services reuse the same eight NWB road-derived links and total nominal 1,200 logical scenario units. They are never physical cables, pipes, sewers, pressure zones, radio links, patient transfers or supply routes.

At compound T+24 modeled availability is power 0.3176, water 0.3793, drainage 0.4423, gas 0.4637, telecom 0.2380, mobility 0.7905, facilities 0.7451 and supply 0.1646; no cited operator source validates those exact values.

causalTrace.summary: Arithmetic ledgers close, but the coastal hazard explanation falsely reports no event forcing while event-attributable impacts accumulate.
notes: Service stage deltas, weighted pressure and matched-no-event person-hour arithmetic close exactly for the matrix.

At coastal T+24 the hazard explanation says 'No event-related hazard forcing is active at this municipality and time' and assigns wind zero effect even though it displays 19.3741 m/s and downstream services are event-degraded.

The cause is inconsistent thresholds: coastal headline wind severity begins above 20 m/s, while service wind pressure begins above 15 m/s. This is a causal/explanation contradiction, not merely absent calibration.
Preparedness and intervention controls remain labeled scenario assumptions; route transfer semantics remain logical-proxy.

recovery72h.summary: Recovery and cumulative burden behave deterministically, but no local operator, water-board, road or healthcare data validates the 72-hour curves.
notes: Coastal T+48 has zero direct hazard and wind but pressure 0.1966, 2,079 affected and 66,829.73 cumulative event-attributable person-hours; the displayed no-forcing causal trace does not explain this inherited damage.

Storm, pluvial, winter, earthquake and wildfire forcing has cleared by T+72 while cumulative burdens reach 401,183.79, 176,352.75, 336,658.66, 223,211.13 and 156,124.55 person-hours respectively; these are proxy integrals, not experienced outage-hours.
Heat retains drought 0.4882 at T+72 while affected population is zero; this threshold result does not establish the absence of residual water, health, peat, agriculture or care burden.

Compound forcing and service pressure remain active at T+72. No real pump controls, provider switching, crew/fuel/spares, route access, hospital capacity, mutual aid or restoration commitment is ingested.
E04 defines flexible roles and initiation targets, not a fixed sequence of interventions through T+72.

findings.summary: The coastal preset says no local event forcing is active while its sub-threshold wind causes material event-attributable service impacts.
findings.evidence: E03 says direct sea-flood consequences do not apply in Drenthe and describes a reception/evacuation role instead. The model correctly screens GM1681 direct water to zero, but canonical T+24 still has wind 19.3741 m/s, headline and peak severity zero, pressure 0.1710, 1,137 affected and 25,558.43 event-attributable service person-hours. Its explanation explicitly says no event forcing is active and gives wind zero effect. At T+48 wind is zero while inherited service damage yields 2,079 affected and 66,829.73 cumulative person-hours. packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:754-763 starts coastal headline wind severity above 20 m/s, while normalized service wind pressure at lines 953-966 starts above 15 m/s.
findings.action: Use one coherent event-attribution contract. If the coastal preset intentionally includes an inland windstorm, label and score that component in the headline/explanation and distinguish it from direct sea inundation. Otherwise suppress local wind damage and represent only explicit, typed reception/evacuation or remote-supply pathways. Add a model/UI gate: an explanation of no event forcing may not coexist with event-attributable service deltas, affected population or person-hours unless a named remote dependency is shown.

findings.summary: Six unrelated hazards reuse one exact neighbourhood order instead of Borger-Odoorn's terrain, water, heat, fire, infrastructure and target mechanisms.
findings.evidence: E02 distinguishes Hondsrug, Hunzedal and peat-area climate mechanisms; E05 distinguishes Hunze and Veenkoloniën water systems; E06 uses seventeen nature-fire parameters per square kilometre. At T+24 severe storm, pluvial flood, heatwave, winter storm, cyberattack and wildfire nevertheless have the identical exact order of all 58 neighbourhoods, starting Borger Buitengebied, 2e Valthermond and Oud Borger. packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3447-3461 applies one municipality/neighbourhood seed and samples none of the official physical mechanisms.
findings.action: Mark computed neighbourhood ranks synthetic/unsupported and prohibit dispatch decisions from them. Prefer a licensed municipal stress-test export when available; otherwise integrate hazard-specific layers: AHN WCS 0.5 m CC0 elevation by cyclical edition, HWH CC BY-SA 4.0 water areas/assets/defences, BRT TOP10NL normally annual CC BY 4.0 land cover, timestamped KNMI event data, and explicit infrastructure/cyber targets. Preserve source edition, resolution, units, no-data, uncertainty and license, and test that hazards may rank differently while service-layer invariance remains exact.

findings.summary: An explicit fire source in Exloo Buitengebied does not control the neighbourhood fire map despite the municipality's large Hondsrug forest areas.
findings.evidence: E03 and E06 support substantial Drenthe nature-fire risk; Staatsbosbeheer's Hondsrug page lists Exloo-Odoorn (1,850 ha) and Gieten-Borger (2,900 ha). In a reproducible synthetic T+24 test, a source at Exloo Buitengebied centre produces municipal direct fire 0.5868, smoke 0.6002 and severity 0.6026. The containing/source neighbourhood ranks only 11/58 at 0.6791, while Borger Buitengebied 6.639 km away ranks first at 0.7105 and the other top-four locations are 5.146–11.864 km away. This test is not evidence of an actual fire.
findings.action: Make an explicit ignition/perimeter control eligible fuel cells and separate flame, smoke and drought. Preferred evidence is an authorized NIPV RIN export; no public bulk API, license or cadence was found. The transparent public fallback is Kadaster BRT TOP10NL OGC (normally annual, CC BY 4.0) plus event-aligned KNMI wind/rain and explicit fuel, moisture, access, extinguishing-water and suppression assumptions. Tests must prioritize source-intersecting eligible cells and expose Unknown where evidence is absent.

findings.summary: The Hondsrug–Hunze–Veenkoloniën water system and 270 public assets are visible context but absent from causal flood, drainage and wastewater behavior.
findings.evidence: E02/E05 establish different high-ground runoff, retention, groundwater, peat-oxidation and canal/pump mechanisms. Current HWH point-in-polygon context contains 247 weirs, 13 sewer pumps, eight surface-water pumps, one sluice and wastewater treatment Tweede Exloërmond; both Hunze en Aa's and Vechtstromen submissions occur. Hunze en Aa's separately reports that Valthermond peat oxidizes roughly 1–2 cm/year above groundwater and that the more-than-50-year-old Nieuw-Buinen sewer pump is planned for replacement in 2027. Yet pluvial T+24 estimates drainage 0.5408 and mobility 0.5457 without catchment, terrain, sewer, storage, control, water level, power/backup, overflow or wastewater topology. Public capacity values have no unit in the app snapshot and cannot calibrate flow.
findings.action: Integrate HWH Kunstwerken/Waterketen/Waterbeheergebieden/Keringen OGC as partial non-causal CC BY-SA 4.0 context, refreshed weekly or by retained object timestamp, and AHN terrain with explicit edition. Seek municipal stress-test/GWSW and water-board hydraulic topology and controls for causal use. Treat the Nieuw-Buinen renewal as dated maintenance context, never a simulated failure probability. Preserve Unknown for unreported capacity units, completeness, state, direction, power/backup and 72-hour dewatering.

findings.summary: Verified Enexis/WMD/Ziggo territories and RDI antenna locations do not calibrate the road-cloned electricity, gas, water or telecom networks.
findings.evidence: A live Stichting Mijn Aansluiting query at the municipal reference point on 2026-09-02 returns Enexis electricity/gas, WMD drinking water and Ziggo fixed media, with public-domain provider-supplied coverage; drainage returns no polygon. RDI contributes 86 sites/171 antennas, including 33 mobile-communication sites/99 antennas and 26 fixed-link sites/45 antennas. The app's physical electricity detail is Liander-only, and every GM1681 service instead reuses eight NWB links with total nominal 1,200. Historical official Enexis WFS documentation says monthly publication, but api.enexis.nl did not resolve and the catalogued S3 asset ZIP returned HTTP 404 on 2026-09-02; current Enexis open data advertises aggregated datasets, not a confirmed physical topology endpoint.
findings.action: Integrate provider territories from https://wiki.service.mijnaansluiting.nl/wiki/spaces/Wiki/pages/693731329 as live Public Domain responsibility context and RDI WFS https://antenneregister.nl/mapserver/wfs/ as deployment-timestamped non-causal site context; the RDI service states no fixed cadence/reuse-license version. Request a publisher-confirmed current Enexis asset endpoint before ingestion and do not revive stale URLs. Use security-reviewed operator exercise connectivity/state for causal electricity, gas, WMD and telecom behavior; otherwise keep the smallest documented synthetic proxy with sensitivity controls and explicit Unknown topology, capacity, backup, crews and restoration.

findings.summary: A sparse road-dependent municipality and its external care access are reduced to eight equal logical links without operational route state.
findings.evidence: The generated official context has eight road links to four neighbours, no railway station and 139 transit stop areas. N34 connects toward Emmen, where E08 identifies the nearest acute hospital. The simulator has no segment closure, traffic, bridge/low-road flooding, snow clearance, bus operation, ambulance travel, evacuation, freight, repair access or alternative-route state; an empty current NDW intersection is not an all-clear. Winter T+24 mobility is 0.1588 and compound T+24 mobility 0.7905, but no public observation calibrates either figure.
findings.action: Use monthly CC0 NWB and manually updated CC0 ProRail as geometry, OVapi GTFS as best-effort schedule context without SLA, and NDW DATEX current situations https://opendata.ndw.nu/actueel_beeld.xml.gz as timestamped CC0-unless-stated observations. Make any feed causal only after explicit scenario-time/geometry matching and data-quality checks. Separate road, rail, transit, ambulance/evacuation and utility graphs; preserve Unknown when there is no operational record.

findings.summary: GM1681 depends on external acute care while local registered sites are not modeled as named continuity, shelter or distribution nodes.
findings.evidence: E01 records 26.8 percent of residents aged 65 or older; E03 says aging, living longer at home and care capacity increase crisis vulnerability. E08 finds no acute hospital inside GM1681 and places Treant Scheper Emmen 13.38 km away by straight-line reference-point distance. Eighteen DUO education and five government/service points are registry context only. Facilities availability is 0.7451 at compound T+24 and 0.2551 at T+72 without ambulance route, acceptance/diversion, staff, beds, care-home/home-care, pharmacy, generator, fuel, school/shelter or support-point state.
findings.action: Retain RIVM v1.1 (2026-07-03, CC0) and daily DUO RIO (CC BY, version unspecified) as dated non-causal context. Add route-aware external acute-care destinations and local reception/distribution facilities only with explicit authorized roles and capacity/state semantics. Seek GHOR/ROAZ, municipal continuity and care-provider exercise data; if security-sensitive or unavailable, show Unknown rather than infer operation from a registry point.

findings.summary: Generic intervention controls do not represent Borger-Odoorn/VRD authority, prerequisites, travel time or resource scarcity through the first 72 hours.
findings.evidence: E04 starts CoPI tasks within 30 minutes, uses ROT for continuity/medium-to-long-term scenarios and scarce resources, and assigns distinct information, operational, mayoral and partner roles. It does not guarantee that a team activates, a water board changes a control, Enexis switches supply, WMD deploys water, an ambulance route is passable, a generator arrives or restoration completes on a fixed timeline. Current generator, pump, traffic and medical-priority controls are time-gated scenario multipliers, not evidence of an actual decision or resource.
findings.action: Keep every control hypothetical. Add an operations timeline that separately records observation/time/confidence, decision authority, action owner, prerequisite, requested/confirmed state, quantity, dispatch/travel delay, effect and handover to recovery. Offer a GM1681/VRD exercise template aligned to E04 without asserting that any municipality, water board, operator, GHOR or hospital has acted.

findings.summary: All non-coastal hazard magnitudes are bounded exercise assumptions; direct-zero river/fire semantics and observed feeds need explicit scope.
findings.evidence: E02/E03 support local relevance of pluvial water, storm, heat/drought, winter disruption, nature fire, vital-service/cyber cascades and induced earthquakes, but do not validate exact magnitudes. The canonical major-river preset is exactly zero through T+72, which is plausible for this selected Rhine/Meuse/IJssel screening but does not exclude Hunze, Veenkoloniën, groundwater, sewer or local-defence water mechanisms. The canonical fire source is 111.247 km away and yields zero flame but 0.2533 smoke at T+24. The canonical Groningen earthquake produces 0.07122 g, severity 0.2226 and 2,343 affected at T+6; by T+24 ground motion is zero but residual damage yields 2,562 affected. E07 validates an event catalogue, not those synthetic ground-motion or fragility values.
findings.action: Label every preset deterministic scenario, never probability, warning or forecast. For observed mode, require explicit event/time/location matching to KNMI radar or earthquake records; for earthquake select a named event and versioned ground-motion/site-response/asset-fragility model; for cyber declare target/system boundary; for fire declare ignition/perimeter/fuel/weather. Show direct local, transported and remote dependency components separately, and keep unmodeled local-water/fire pathways Unknown rather than converting a scoped zero into an all-clear.

findings.summary: Identity, population, neighbourhood, place, settlement and public-context provenance are inspectable and null-safe.
findings.evidence: E01 matches GM1681/Borger-Odoorn and the official 2025 totals. All 58 neighbourhoods, 25 BAG places and 31 BRT settlements load; the nine-person CBS rounded reconciliation is disclosed. Zero population remains exact. Missing district heat/public charging, absent drainage territory and empty NDW context remain null/Unknown. HWH, RDI, RIVM, DUO, provider and transport snapshots retain publisher, URL, retrieval/edition and licence/no-licence caveats and do not affect the simulation unless explicitly declared.
findings.action: Retain edition, retrieval time, licence, coverage, no-data and affectsSimulation semantics. Refresh each public adapter at its publisher cadence and rerun generated-data plus focused/national model gates after every snapshot.

findings.summary: The complete deterministic and layer-invariance contract passes for Borger-Odoorn despite the identified semantic and calibration defects.
findings.evidence: The mandatory harness passes 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services; intensity-zero output is exact zero; local population, demand and delivery balances reconcile; causal arithmetic closes; person-hours are event-attributable against a matched no-event baseline; all layer selections preserve hazard/state; the official zero population is retained; and every route declares logical-proxy semantics.
findings.action: Retain these assertions as regression gates while fixing the coastal explanation/impact invariant and adding authoritative spatial adapters; do not weaken deterministic, exact-zero, reconciliation or layer-invariance checks to conceal calibration gaps.

corrections.summary: Make coastal headline, explanation and event-attributable service impacts causally coherent for inland GM1681.
corrections.validation: Regression values before correction: canonical GM1681 coastal T+24 flood=0, wind=19.374060782251444 m/s, severity=0, peakSeverity=0, pressure=0.1710, affected=1,137, event-attributable person-hours=25,558.43; T+48 wind=0, severity=0, affected=2,079, person-hours=66,829.73. Align the >20 m/s headline and >15 m/s service thresholds or explicitly distinguish an inland storm component. Assert that 'No event-related hazard forcing' implies zero event-attributable service deltas/affected/person-hours unless an individually named remote pathway contributes; UI must distinguish direct sea inundation, inland weather and reception/evacuation demand.

corrections.summary: Replace shared neighbourhood ranking and source-insensitive fire allocation with versioned hazard-specific evidence.
corrections.validation: Before correction, six canonical T+24 presets share the complete 58-neighbourhood order; the synthetic Exloo Buitengebied fire source ranks 11/58 while a neighbourhood 6.639 km away ranks first. Mark ranks unsupported until sourced. Prefer authorized NIPV RIN; otherwise use BRT TOP10NL OGC https://api.pdok.nl/kadaster/brt-top10nl/ogc/v1 (normally annual, CC BY 4.0), AHN WCS https://service.pdok.nl/rws/actueel-hoogtebestand-nederland/wcs/v1_0?SERVICE=WCS&REQUEST=GetCapabilities (0.5 m, CC0, cyclical edition), HWH layers and event-aligned KNMI forcing. Tests must allow hazard-specific order, keep service-layer invariance exact, prioritize a source-intersecting eligible fire cell and preserve Unknown no-data.

corrections.summary: Add typed GM1681 water, operator, telecom, mobility and facility context without inventing operational topology.
corrections.validation: HWH Kunstwerken https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-kunstwerken-imwa/ogc/v2 and Waterketen https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1 are partial CC BY-SA 4.0 point context with variable completeness/object dates; provider WMS/WFS is live Public Domain territory context; RDI WFS has no stated fixed cadence/licence; RIVM is v1.1 2026-07-03 CC0; DUO RIO is daily CC BY (version unspecified); NWB is monthly CC0; ProRail is manually updated CC0; NDW is live CC0 unless stated. Keep all affectsSimulation=false until topology, unit-correct capacity, state, role, backup and decision semantics are authorized.

corrections.summary: Make GM1681 first-72-hour operational ownership, prerequisites and Unknown recovery inputs explicit.
corrections.validation: Represent observation, confidence, decision authority, action owner, prerequisite, requested/confirmed status, quantity, travel/dispatch delay, effect and recovery handover separately. Assert that generic controls never imply a real VRD, municipality, water-board, operator, GHOR or hospital action. At T+72 expose residual hazard, each service, system pressure, affected population and cumulative event-attributable proxy together; zero affected may not be labeled complete recovery while material residual hazard/service pressure remains.

residualLimitations: The simulator is a deterministic planning stress test, not a KNMI forecast, official warning, probability estimate, live incident picture, casualty model or operator outage forecast.
No selected hydraulic stress-test/LIWO footprint, source, defence, arrival, duration, water level or recession grid is ingested for GM1681; internal flood stress is not measured metres.
Direct zero in the major-river/coastal/fire screens applies only to the named synthetic pathway and must not erase local water, reception/evacuation, smoke or unmodeled fire risk.
CBS neighbourhoods and deterministic seeds do not resolve Hondsrug terrain, low Hunze/Veenkoloniën areas, peat, buildings, paving, shade, vegetation, households, visitors or individual vulnerability.
The HWH national aggregation is partial; 270 points cannot be interpreted as a complete connected surface-water, sewer or wastewater system, and its capacity values lack units in the snapshot.

No public causal Enexis feeder/switching, WMD pipe/pressure-zone/reserve, gas pressure-district, sewer, Ziggo/mobile backhaul or operator restoration topology is available and authorized in the model.
Provider polygons identify responsibility at one reference point, not complete coverage, physical connectivity, capacity or state; no drainage polygon does not mean no responsible authority.
RDI antenna points do not establish operator, radio coverage, backhaul, traffic, power/backup, damage, congestion, availability or restoration.
All eight service layers reuse eight road-derived logical corridors and cannot be interpreted as cables, pipes, sewers, pressure zones, radio backhaul, patient transfers or food routes.
Static NWB, ProRail and GTFS inputs do not establish live closure, traffic, timetable operation, evacuation capacity, ambulance travel or repair access; an empty NDW snapshot is not an all-clear.
No acute hospital is inside GM1681 in E08; straight-line distance to Treant Scheper Emmen is not ambulance travel time, acceptance, staffing, bed capacity or diversion status.
DUO and government-service records do not establish command or shelter status; facilities/supply lack verified care-home, pharmacy, support-point, stock, depot, vehicle, staff and continuity state.
Wildfire lacks a local perimeter, fuel/moisture surface, wind-aware spread, suppression state, extinguishing water and access; the Exloo diagnostic is explicitly synthetic.
Earthquake lacks a selected event, ground-motion surface, local site response and asset fragility; a catalogue event is observed context, not scenario probability.
Generic preparedness, demand, backup, network, repair and intervention multipliers are scenario controls rather than observed GM1681 resources or commitments.
Event-attributable essential-service person-hours is a matched-no-event all-service availability proxy, not experienced outage-hours, casualties, displacement or welfare loss.

Six-hour checkpoints can miss cloudbursts, water-level/control changes, route restrictions, fire spread and dispatch; 72 hours excludes prolonged contamination, care effects, peat/subsidence, displacement, ecological loss and reconstruction.
